author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **4.5.2** to **7.9.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.9.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a ``[run] core`` configuration setting to specify the measurement core,
  which was previously only available through the COVERAGE_CORE environment
  variable. Finishes `issue 1746`_.

- Fixed incorrect rendering of f-strings with doubled braces, closing `issue
  1980`_.

- If the C tracer core can't be imported, a warning ("no-ctracer") is issued
  with the reason.

- The C tracer core extension module now conforms to `PEP 489`_, closing `issue
  1977`_.  Thanks, `Adam Turner <pull 1978_>`_.

- Fixed a "ValueError: min() arg is an empty sequence" error caused by strange
  empty modules, found by `oss-fuzz`_.

.. _issue 1746: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1746
.. _issue 1977: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1977
.. _pull 1978: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1978
.. _issue 1980: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1980
.. _PEP 489: https://peps.python.org/pep-0489
.. _oss-fuzz: https://google.github.io/oss-fuzz/


.. _changes_7-8-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.8.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- Wheels are provided for Windows ARM64 on Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13.
  Thanks, `Finn Womack <pull 1972_>`_.

.. _issue 1971: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1971
.. _pull 1972: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1972

.. _changes_7-8-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.8.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- A number of EncodingWarnings were fixed that could appear if you've enabled
  PYTHONWARNDEFAULTENCODING, fixing `issue 1966`_.  Thanks, `Henry Schreiner
  <pull 1967_>`_.

- Fixed a race condition when using sys.monitoring with free-threading Python,
  closing `issue 1970`_.

.. _issue 1966: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1966
.. _pull 1967: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1967
.. _issue 1970: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1970

.. _changes_7-8-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.8.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a new ``source_dirs`` setting for symmetry with the existing
  ``source_pkgs`` setting. It's preferable to the existing ``source`` setting,
  because you'll get a clear error when directories don't exist. Fixes `issue
  1942`_.  Thanks, `Jeremy Fleischman <pull 1943_>`_.

- Fix: the PYTHONSAFEPATH environment variable new in Python 3.11 is properly
  supported, closing `issue 1696`_.  Thanks, `Philipp A. <pull 1700_>`_.  This
  works properly except for a detail when using the ``coverage`` command on
  Windows.  There you can use ``python -m coverage`` instead if you need exact
  emulation.

.. _issue 1696: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1696
.. _pull 1700: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1700
.. _issue 1942: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1942
.. _pull 1943: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1943

.. _changes_7-7-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.7.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- A few small tweaks to the sys.monitoring support for Python 3.14.  Please
  test!


.. _changes_7-7-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.7.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- The Coverage object has a new method, :meth:`.Coverage.branch_stats` for
  getting simple branch information for a module.  Closes `issue 1888`_.

- The :class:`Coverage constructor<.Coverage>` now has a ``plugins`` parameter
  for passing in plugin objects directly, thanks to `Alex Gaynor <pull
  1919_>`_.

- Many constant tests in if statements are now recognized as being optimized
  away.  For example, previously ``if 13:`` would have been considered a branch
  with one path not taken.  Now it is understood as always true and no coverage
  is missing.

- The experimental sys.monitoring support now works for branch coverage if you
  are using Python 3.14.0 alpha 6 or newer.  This should reduce the overhead
  coverage.py imposes on your test suite. Set the environment variable
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` to try it out.

- Confirmed support for PyPy 3.11. Thanks Michał Górny.

.. _issue 1888: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1888
.. _pull 1919: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1919


.. _changes_7-6-12:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.12
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some aarch64 distributions were missing (`issue 1927`_).  These are now
  building reliably.

.. _issue 1927: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1927

.. _changes_7-6-11:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.11
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: a memory leak in CTracer has been fixed.  The details are in `issue
  1924`_ and `pytest-dev 676`_.  This should reduce the memory footprint for
  everyone even if it hadn't caused a problem before.

- We now ship a py3-none-any.whl wheel file.  Thanks, `Russell Keith-Magee
  <pull 1914_>`_.

.. _pull 1914: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1914
.. _issue 1924: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1924
.. _pytest-dev 676: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/676

.. _changes_7-6-10:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.10
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some descriptions of missing branches in HTML and LCOV reports were
  incorrect when multi-line statements were involved (`issue 1874`_ and `issue
  1875`_).  These are now fixed.

- Fix: Python 3.14 `defers evaluation of annotations <pep649_>`_ by moving them
  into separate code objects.  That code is rarely executed, so coverage.py
  would mark them as missing, as reported in `issue 1908`_.  Now they are
  ignored by coverage automatically.

- Fixed an obscure and mysterious problem on PyPy 3.10 seemingly involving
  mocks, imports, and trace functions: `issue 1902`_.  To be honest, I don't
  understand the problem or the solution, but ``git bisect`` helped find it,
  and now it's fixed.

- Docs: re-wrote the :ref:`subprocess` page to put multiprocessing first and to
  highlight the correct use of :class:`multiprocessing.Pool
  <python:multiprocessing.pool.Pool>`.

.. _issue 1875: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1875

.. _changes_7-6-8:
   ```

- Fix: the LCOV report code assumed that a branch line that took no branches
  meant that the entire line was unexecuted.  This isn't true in a few cases:
  the line might always raise an exception, or might have been optimized away.
  Fixes `issue 1896`_.

- Fix: similarly, the HTML report will now explain that a line that jumps to
  none of its expected destinations must have always raised an exception.
  Previously, it would say something nonsensical like, "line 4 didn't jump to
  line 5 because line 4 was never true, and it didn't jump to line 7 because
  line 4 was always true."  This was also shown in `issue 1896`_.

This PR updates [pytest-cov](https://pypi.org/project/pytest-cov) from **2.6.1** to **6.2.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 6.2.1
   ```
   ------------------

* Added a version requirement for pytest's pluggy dependency (1.2.0, released 2023-06-21) that has the required new-style hookwrapper API.
* Removed deprecated license classifier (packaging).
* Disabled coverage warnings in two more situations where they have no value:

  * "module-not-measured" in workers
  * "already-imported" in subprocesses
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.2.0
   ```
   ------------------

* The plugin now adds 3 rules in the filter warnings configuration to prevent common coverage warnings being raised as obscure errors::

    default:unclosed database in <sqlite3.Connection object at:ResourceWarning
    once::PytestCovWarning
    once::CoverageWarning

  This fixes most of the bad interactions that are occurring on pytest 8.4 with ``filterwarnings=error``.

  The plugin will check if there already matching rules for the 3 categories
  (``ResourceWarning``, ``PytestCovWarning``, ``CoverageWarning``) and message (``unclosed database in <sqlite3.Connection object at``) before adding the filters.

  This means you can have this in your pytest configuration for complete oblivion (not recommended, if that is not clear)::

    filterwarnings = [
        "error",
        "ignore:unclosed database in <sqlite3.Connection object at:ResourceWarning",
        "ignore::PytestCovWarning",
        "ignore::CoverageWarning",
    ]
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.1.1
   ```
   ------------------

* Fixed breakage that occurs when ``--cov-context`` and the ``no_cover`` marker are used together.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.1.0
   ```
   ------------------

* Change terminal output to use full width lines for the coverage header.
  Contributed by Tsvika Shapira in `678 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/678>`_.
* Removed unnecessary CovFailUnderWarning. Fixes `675 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/675>`_.
* Fixed the term report not using the precision specified via ``--cov-precision``.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0.0
   ```
   ------------------

* Updated various documentation inaccuracies, especially on subprocess handling.
* Changed fail under checks to use the precision set in the coverage configuration.
  Now it will perform the check just like ``coverage report`` would.
* Added a ``--cov-precision`` cli option that can override the value set in your coverage configuration.
* Dropped support for now EOL Python 3.8.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.0.0
   ```
   ------------------

* Removed support for xdist rsync (now deprecated).
  Contributed by Matthias Reichenbach in `623 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/623>`_.
* Switched docs theme to Furo.
* Various legacy Python cleanup and CI improvements.
  Contributed by Christian Clauss and Hugo van Kemenade in
  `630 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/630>`_,
  `631 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/631>`_,
  `632 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/632>`_ and
  `633 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/633>`_.
* Added a ``pyproject.toml`` example in the docs.
  Contributed by Dawn James in `626 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/626>`_.
* Modernized project's pre-commit hooks to use ruff. Initial POC contributed by
  Christian Clauss in `584 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/584>`_.
* Dropped support for Python 3.7.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.1.0
   ```
   ------------------

* Updated CI with new Pythons and dependencies.
* Removed rsyncdir support. This makes pytest-cov compatible with xdist 3.0.
  Contributed by Sorin Sbarnea in `558 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/558>`_.
* Optimized summary generation to not be performed if no reporting is active (for example,
  when ``--cov-report=''`` is used without ``--cov-fail-under``).
  Contributed by Jonathan Stewmon in `589 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/589>`_.
* Added support for JSON reporting.
  Contributed by Matthew Gamble in `582 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/582>`_.
* Refactored code to use f-strings.
  Contributed by Mark Mayo in `572 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/572>`_.
* Fixed a skip in the test suite for some old xdist.
  Contributed by a bunch of people in `565 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/565>`_.
* Dropped support for Python 3.6.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.0.0
   ```
   ------------------

**Note that this release drops support for multiprocessing.**


* `--cov-fail-under` no longer causes `pytest --collect-only` to fail
  Contributed by Zac Hatfield-Dodds in `511 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/511>`_.
* Dropped support for multiprocessing (mostly because `issue 82408 <https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/82408>`_). This feature was
  mostly working but very broken in certain scenarios and made the test suite very flaky and slow.

  There is builtin multiprocessing support in coverage and you can migrate to that. All you need is this in your
  ``.coveragerc``::

    [run]
    concurrency = multiprocessing
    parallel = true
    sigterm = true
* Fixed deprecation in ``setup.py`` by trying to import setuptools before distutils.
  Contributed by Ben Greiner in `545 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/545>`_.
* Removed undesirable new lines that were displayed while reporting was disabled.
  Contributed by Delgan in `540 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/540>`_.
* Documentation fixes.
  Contributed by Andre Brisco in `543 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/543>`_
  and Colin O'Dell in `525 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/525>`_.
* Added support for LCOV output format via `--cov-report=lcov`. Only works with coverage 6.3+.
  Contributed by Christian Fetzer in `536 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/536>`_.
* Modernized pytest hook implementation.
  Contributed by Bruno Oliveira in `549 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/549>`_
  and Ronny Pfannschmidt in `550 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/550>`_.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.0.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Note that this release drops support for Python 2.7 and Python 3.5.**

* Added support for Python 3.10 and updated various test dependencies.
  Contributed by Hugo van Kemenade in
  `500 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/500>`_.
* Switched from Travis CI to GitHub Actions. Contributed by Hugo van Kemenade in
  `494 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/494>`_ and
  `495 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/495>`_.
* Add a ``--cov-reset`` CLI option.
  Contributed by Danilo Šegan in
  `459 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/459>`_.
* Improved validation of ``--cov-fail-under`` CLI option.
  Contributed by ... Ronny Pfannschmidt's desire for skark in
  `480 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/480>`_.
* Dropped Python 2.7 support.
  Contributed by Thomas Grainger in
  `488 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/488>`_.
* Updated trove classifiers. Contributed by Michał Bielawski in
  `481 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/481>`_.
* Reverted change for `toml` requirement.
  Contributed by Thomas Grainger in
  `477 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/pull/477>`_.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.12.1
   ```
   -------------------

* Changed the `toml` requirement to be always be directly required (instead of being required through a coverage extra).
  This fixes issues with pip-compile (`pip-tools1300 <https://github.com/jazzband/pip-tools/issues/1300>`_).

This pull request introduces several changes to the codebase, focusing on simplifying the build process, enhancing the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) with new features, and improving semantic analysis. The most significant updates include removing LLVM host triple and data layout probing, adding support for `print` expressions, refactoring `for` and `if-else` constructs, and enhancing semantic validation for `for` loops.

### Build Process Simplification:
* [`build.rs`](diffhunk://#diff-d0d98998092552a1d3259338c2c71e118a5b8343dd4703c0c7f552ada7f9cb42L3-L34): Removed LLVM host triple and data layout probing logic, simplifying the build script and eliminating reliance on environment variables.
* [`src/codegen/llvm_utils.rs`](diffhunk://#diff-c37ef67dc832ae3a934a9f2f04efa355cdb4e04d04d4c7bc9b4e1c930505554eL32-R34): Hardcoded target triple and data layout in the `generate_header` function, removing dynamic generation via environment variables.

### AST Enhancements:
* [`src/ast_nodes/expression.rs`](diffhunk://#diff-3d16cd20f9c16cd9c6d124bcda24d45bdb0d05ed0ea05a90e90b9e105e521962R11): Added `PrintNode` to the `Expression` enum and implemented methods for creating `print` expressions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3d16cd20f9c16cd9c6d124bcda24d45bdb0d05ed0ea05a90e90b9e105e521962R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3d16cd20f9c16cd9c6d124bcda24d45bdb0d05ed0ea05a90e90b9e105e521962R36) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3d16cd20f9c16cd9c6d124bcda24d45bdb0d05ed0ea05a90e90b9e105e521962L101-R105) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b12268da5b4824b54e95ff19307f2e0641c6b871ebb7f8dcffede68a5244ae93R123-R126)
* [`src/parser.lalrpop`](diffhunk://#diff-e54fbaba2e815faa0451f69cf4dede45a89f11e71c5ab14e406aa923c6902de7L296-R290): Added grammar rules for `print` expressions and updated the `PrimaryExpr` production. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e54fbaba2e815faa0451f69cf4dede45a89f11e71c5ab14e406aa923c6902de7L296-R290) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e54fbaba2e815faa0451f69cf4dede45a89f11e71c5ab14e406aa923c6902de7L311-R307)

### Refactoring Constructs:
* [`src/ast_nodes/expression.rs`](diffhunk://#diff-3d16cd20f9c16cd9c6d124bcda24d45bdb0d05ed0ea05a90e90b9e105e521962L62-R65): Refactored `new_for_loop` to use an iterable expression instead of `start` and `end` parameters. author: fjebaker
body:
@DariusMichienzi here's the parameter patching. An example:
```julia
model = PowerLaw() + PowerLaw()

function patcher!(p)
    # this can be any arbitrary function, accessing the parameters of the model as you would otherwise
    p.a1.K = p.a2.K / 2
    # even weird things
    p.a1.a = sqrt(p.a2.a) + sin(p.a1.a)
end

patched_model = ParameterPatch(model; patch = patcher!)

# i'd recommend freezing the parameters you patch, to avoid fitting problems
patched_model.a1.K.frozen = true
patched_model.a1.a.frozen = true
```
In the future I'll make it do that freezing automatically.

That's all you need to do. Then use `patched_model` as before!

I haven't programmed the user-interface bits yet, so that or how things are being patched is a little opaque at the moment, but I have added an `apply_patch!` function that you can give a `ParameterPatch` model to. This function will apply whatever your patch function does to your `FitParam` model. In practice, you'd want to do
```julia
result = fit(prob, LevenbergMarquadt())

update_model!(patched_model, result)
apply_patch!(patched_model)
```
And then inspect the overall model as usual.

Hope that helps!

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

OpenTelemetry logging was not working for worker services because the worker CLI was missing the `--log-otlp` parameter that other services (experience-api, status-api, worker-dal-api, status-processor) already had. This meant that even when OTEL was properly configured in Helm charts, worker services couldn't enable OTEL logging.

## Root Cause

The worker service callback in `src/manman/worker/main.py` was calling:
```python
setup_logging(service_name="worker")  # Missing enable_otel parameter
```

While other services were calling:
```python
setup_logging(service_name="service-name", enable_otel=log_otlp)
```

## Solution

Added the missing `log_otlp` parameter to the worker service Typer callback, making it consistent with other services:

```python
log_otlp: Annotated[
    bool,
    typer.Option(
        envvar="MANMAN_LOG_OTLP", help="Enable OpenTelemetry OTLP logging"
    ),
] = False,
```

And updated the logging setup to use it:
```python
setup_logging(service_name="worker", enable_otel=log_otlp)
```

## Benefits

- ✅ Worker services now support both `--log-otlp` CLI flag and `MANMAN_LOG_OTLP` environment variable
- ✅ Consistent OTEL logging interface across all ManMan services
- ✅ Complete observability coverage for the distributed system
- ✅ No breaking changes - OTEL logging remains disabled by default

## Testing

- All existing tests pass (52 passed, 1 skipped)
- Verified OTEL handlers are properly configured when `--log-otlp` is enabled
- Confirmed environment variable `MANMAN_LOG_OTLP` works correctly
- Tested deployment scenario simulation with proper OTEL endpoint configuration

Fixes #116.

This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **4.5.3** to **7.9.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.9.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a ``[run] core`` configuration setting to specify the measurement core,
  which was previously only available through the COVERAGE_CORE environment
  variable. Finishes `issue 1746`_.

- Fixed incorrect rendering of f-strings with doubled braces, closing `issue
  1980`_.

- If the C tracer core can't be imported, a warning ("no-ctracer") is issued
  with the reason.

- The C tracer core extension module now conforms to `PEP 489`_, closing `issue
  1977`_.  Thanks, `Adam Turner <pull 1978_>`_.

- Fixed a "ValueError: min() arg is an empty sequence" error caused by strange
  empty modules, found by `oss-fuzz`_.

.. _issue 1746: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1746
.. _issue 1977: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1977
.. _pull 1978: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1978
.. _issue 1980: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1980
.. _PEP 489: https://peps.python.org/pep-0489
.. _oss-fuzz: https://google.github.io/oss-fuzz/


.. _changes_7-8-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.8.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- Wheels are provided for Windows ARM64 on Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13.
  Thanks, `Finn Womack <pull 1972_>`_.

.. _issue 1971: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1971
.. _pull 1972: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1972

.. _changes_7-8-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.8.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- A number of EncodingWarnings were fixed that could appear if you've enabled
  PYTHONWARNDEFAULTENCODING, fixing `issue 1966`_.  Thanks, `Henry Schreiner
  <pull 1967_>`_.

- Fixed a race condition when using sys.monitoring with free-threading Python,
  closing `issue 1970`_.

.. _issue 1966: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1966
.. _pull 1967: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1967
.. _issue 1970: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1970

.. _changes_7-8-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.8.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a new ``source_dirs`` setting for symmetry with the existing
  ``source_pkgs`` setting. It's preferable to the existing ``source`` setting,
  because you'll get a clear error when directories don't exist. Fixes `issue
  1942`_.  Thanks, `Jeremy Fleischman <pull 1943_>`_.

- Fix: the PYTHONSAFEPATH environment variable new in Python 3.11 is properly
  supported, closing `issue 1696`_.  Thanks, `Philipp A. <pull 1700_>`_.  This
  works properly except for a detail when using the ``coverage`` command on
  Windows.  There you can use ``python -m coverage`` instead if you need exact
  emulation.

.. _issue 1696: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1696
.. _pull 1700: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1700
.. _issue 1942: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1942
.. _pull 1943: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1943

.. _changes_7-7-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.7.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- A few small tweaks to the sys.monitoring support for Python 3.14.  Please
  test!


.. _changes_7-7-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.7.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- The Coverage object has a new method, :meth:`.Coverage.branch_stats` for
  getting simple branch information for a module.  Closes `issue 1888`_.

- The :class:`Coverage constructor<.Coverage>` now has a ``plugins`` parameter
  for passing in plugin objects directly, thanks to `Alex Gaynor <pull
  1919_>`_.

- Many constant tests in if statements are now recognized as being optimized
  away.  For example, previously ``if 13:`` would have been considered a branch
  with one path not taken.  Now it is understood as always true and no coverage
  is missing.

- The experimental sys.monitoring support now works for branch coverage if you
  are using Python 3.14.0 alpha 6 or newer.  This should reduce the overhead
  coverage.py imposes on your test suite. Set the environment variable
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` to try it out.

- Confirmed support for PyPy 3.11. Thanks Michał Górny.

.. _issue 1888: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1888
.. _pull 1919: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1919


.. _changes_7-6-12:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.12
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some aarch64 distributions were missing (`issue 1927`_).  These are now
  building reliably.

.. _issue 1927: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1927

.. _changes_7-6-11:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.11
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: a memory leak in CTracer has been fixed.  The details are in `issue
  1924`_ and `pytest-dev 676`_.  This should reduce the memory footprint for
  everyone even if it hadn't caused a problem before.

- We now ship a py3-none-any.whl wheel file.  Thanks, `Russell Keith-Magee
  <pull 1914_>`_.

.. _pull 1914: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1914
.. _issue 1924: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1924
.. _pytest-dev 676: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/676

.. _changes_7-6-10:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.10
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some descriptions of missing branches in HTML and LCOV reports were
  incorrect when multi-line statements were involved (`issue 1874`_ and `issue
  1875`_).  These are now fixed.

- Fix: Python 3.14 `defers evaluation of annotations <pep649_>`_ by moving them
  into separate code objects.  That code is rarely executed, so coverage.py
  would mark them as missing, as reported in `issue 1908`_.  Now they are
  ignored by coverage automatically.

- Fixed an obscure and mysterious problem on PyPy 3.10 seemingly involving
  mocks, imports, and trace functions: `issue 1902`_.  To be honest, I don't
  understand the problem or the solution, but ``git bisect`` helped find it,
  and now it's fixed.

- Docs: re-wrote the :ref:`subprocess` page to put multiprocessing first and to
  highlight the correct use of :class:`multiprocessing.Pool
  <python:multiprocessing.pool.Pool>`.

.. _issue 1874: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1874
.. _issue 1875: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1875
.. _issue 1902: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1902
.. _issue 1908: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1908
.. _pep649: https://docs.python.org/3.14/whatsnew/3.14.html#whatsnew314-pep649


.. _changes_7-6-9:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.9
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: `Tomas Uribe fixed <pull 1901_>`_ a performance problem in the XML
  report.  Large code bases should produce XML reports much faster now.

.. _pull 1901: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1901


.. _changes_7-6-8:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.8
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the LCOV report code assumed that a branch line that took no branches
  meant that the entire line was unexecuted.  This isn't true in a few cases:
  the line might always raise an exception, or might have been optimized away.
  Fixes `issue 1896`_.

- Fix: similarly, the HTML report will now explain that a line that jumps to
  none of its expected destinations must have always raised an exception.
  Previously, it would say something nonsensical like, "line 4 didn't jump to
  line 5 because line 4 was never true, and it didn't jump to line 7 because
  line 4 was always true."  This was also shown in `issue 1896`_.

.. _issue 1896: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1896


.. _changes_7-6-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ugh, the other assert from 7.6.5 can also be encountered in the wild,
  so it's been restored to a conditional.  Sorry for the churn.


.. _changes_7-6-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.6
   ```

author: demonha
body:
**Problem**

There is currently no validation or type coercion for the input document. This means any arbitrary input is accepted, and we implicitly assume it to be a valid OpenAPI document. This can lead to runtime issues and unreliable behavior when the input is malformed or doesn't conform to the expected structure.

**Solution**

This PR introduces a coercion step for the input document, transforming it into a structure that aligns with the OpenAPI schema. By doing so, even loosely structured or partially invalid inputs are normalized before validation. The result is that the document consistently passes strict OpenAPI schema checks, improving reliability and robustness.

This PR addresses the requirement to update the MSP430 emulator task list with comprehensive instruction coverage based on official Texas Instruments documentation, including all MSP430(X) instructions and emulated instructions.

## Changes Made

### 📚 **Enhanced Existing Instruction Tasks (Phases 4-6)**
- Added specific TI documentation references to all instruction tasks using format: `SLAU445I Section 4.6.2.X`
- Updated task dependencies to maintain proper sequencing
- Added missing arithmetic instructions (ADDC, SUBC, DADD) to Phase 4
- Enhanced logical operations coverage with proper TI section references

### 🆕 **New Phase 8.5: Comprehensive MSP430 Instruction Coverage**
Added systematic coverage of the complete MSP430 instruction set:

**Core MSP430 Instructions (51 total from SLAU445I Section 4.6.2):**
- ✅ Implementation status tracking for all arithmetic, logical, data movement, rotation, and control flow instructions
- ⚠️ Gap identification for missing instructions (CALL, RET, RETI, etc.)

**MSP430X Extended Instructions (37 total from SLAU445I Section 4.6.3):**
- Extended arithmetic: ADDX, ADDCX, SUBX, SUBCX, CMPX, DADDX
- Extended logical: ANDX, BICX, BISX, BITX, XORX  
- Extended data movement: MOVX, PUSHX, POPX, SWPBX, SXTX
- Extended rotation: RLAX, RLCX, RRAX, RRCX, RRUM, RRUX, etc.
- Multiple register operations: POPM, PUSHM

**MSP430X Address Instructions (11 total from SLAU445I Section 4.6.4):**
- 20-bit addressing support: ADDA, BRA, CALLA, MOVA, RETA, etc.

### 🔄 **New Task 6.5: Emulated Instruction Implementation and Validation**
Complete coverage of emulated instructions:
- All 25 standard emulated instructions from SLAU445I Table 4-7
- Extended emulated instructions from SLAU445I Table 4-15
- Validation requirements for instruction equivalence and cycle counts

### 📋 **Policy Compliance Framework**
Added comprehensive policy compliance guidance:
- **TI Documentation Requirements**: Mandatory references to SLAU445I, SLAU131Y, SLASEC4D
- **Code Standards**: File organization, naming conventions, test coverage requirements
- **Development Workflow**: Pre-commit validation commands and build integration
- **Task Documentation Standards**: Required TI reference format and validation

## Key Metrics

- **37 TI documentation references** added across all instruction tasks
- **108 specific instruction citations** covering Sections 4.6.2, 4.6.3, and 4.6.4
- **Complete coverage** of all MSP430(X) instructions documented in official TI specifications
- **Minimal changes approach** - enhanced existing structure without disrupting working phases

## Example Enhancement

Before:
```markdown
### Task 4.1: Basic Arithmetic Instructions ✅ COMPLETED
Implement fundamental arithmetic operations (ADD, SUB, CMP) with proper flag handling.
```

After:
```markdown
### Task 4.1: Basic Arithmetic Instructions ✅ COMPLETED
Implement fundamental arithmetic operations (ADD, SUB, CMP) with proper flag handling.

**TI Documentation References:**
- SLAU445I Section 4.6.2.2 ADD - Add source to destination  
- SLAU445I Section 4.6.2.46 SUB - Subtract source from destination
- SLAU445I Section 4.6.2.14 CMP - Compare source and destination
```

The task list now provides complete coverage of all MSP430(X) instructions as specified in official Texas Instruments documentation, with integrated policy compliance guidance ensuring future development adheres to repository standards.

Fixes #175.

author: alexdlukens
body:
Hello,

Was running starlette-admin from behind Nginx in Kubernetes. 
HTTPS is configured on NGINX, and the backing application where starlette-admin is running uses HTTP.

Ran into issue #400 where starlette-admin was serving HTTP content, `This request has been blocked; the content must be served over HTTPS.`. 

I think a solution to this is to use relative routes, by removing the host and protocol portion of all links used. E.g. instead of `http://example.com/statics/css/tabler.min.css`, use `/statics/css/tabler.min.css`. 

I did this in the PR by using the `strip_host_filter` function. I use this in the Jinja templates and in some areas of the python code.

Edited testcases that assert on absolute routes in 6a2c435. 

Best,
Alex

author: marcuscastelo
body:
This pull request refactors the `isSearchCached` function in `src/modules/search/application/searchCache.ts` to optimize search cache lookups and prevent a full table scan.

**What was changed:**
- Updated `isSearchCached` to query only for the specific search string using `.eq('search', search.toLowerCase())`, eliminating the previous approach of fetching all rows and filtering in-memory.
- Removed unused imports and unnecessary optional chaining.
- Ensured the function returns `true` if a matching row exists, `false` otherwise.
- Ran the full check suite (`npm run check`) to ensure all tests and type checks pass.

**Why:**
- The previous implementation caused excessive data transfer and slow performance as the `cached_searches` table grew.
- This change addresses performance and data consumption concerns, as noted in audit documentation.

**Context:**
- No direct tests for `isSearchCached` were found, but the change was validated by running the project's check suite.
- No breaking changes introduced.

closes #770

body:
This pull request introduces enhancements to edge data handling in the `CommandController` and `useStore`. The changes focus on improving the management and restoration of edge data during operations, as well as adding support for edge data updates during drag operations.

Fixes #48 

### Enhancements to edge data handling in `CommandController`:

* **Preservation of original edge data**: Added functionality to store the original edge data in a `Map` for later restoration. (`src/controllers/CommandController.ts`, [src/controllers/CommandController.tsR552-R559](diffhunk://#diff-0cbf88e2986264c55b2b783b4c559e22ed6980a3a19e3447545bcd99e1e8d9c4R552-R559))
* **Updating edge data during operations**: Implemented logic to update edge data based on operations, ensuring changes are applied correctly to the `edges` state. (`src/controllers/CommandController.ts`, [src/controllers/CommandController.tsR582-R600](diffhunk://#diff-0cbf88e2986264c55b2b783b4c559e22ed6980a3a19e3447545bcd99e1e8d9c4R582-R600))
* **Restoration of edge data**: Added functionality to restore edge data to its original state using the stored `Map` during specific operations. (`src/controllers/CommandController.ts`, [src/controllers/CommandController.tsR626-R639](diffhunk://#diff-0cbf88e2986264c55b2b783b4c559e22ed6980a3a19e3447545bcd99e1e8d9c4R626-R639))

### Enhancements to drag operations in `useStore`:

* **Edge data updates during drag operations**: Introduced logic to update edge data (e.g., `controlPoints` and `conditionLabelOffset`) during drag operations, ensuring the changes are reflected accurately in the state. (`src/store/index.ts`, [src/store/index.tsR984-R1028](diffhunk://#diff-6617a8982092b70693d565d280deb361a2c860ca52f2a1d23f537ce5d276023bR984-R1028))

author: parcly-taxel
body:
* `volume_F_pos` is totally unused and `volume_G_pos` only appears in two calc steps which are still true when `volume G = 0`. They can probably be removed.
* The blueprint says that `S` is the smallest integer such that the ranges of `σ₁, σ₂` are contained in `[-S, S]` **and** `F, G` are contained in the ball `B(o, D^S / 4)`. Yet `defaultS` as currently defined does not take into account the latter property. We fix this, after the aforementioned provisional removal of `volume_FG_pos`, by adding `IsBounded F` and `IsBounded G` to `PreProofData` and **unifying** `ProofData` into it, so that only `ProofData` remains. The ball inclusion can be proven from `IsBounded F` and `IsBounded G`.

author: meleksomai
body:
This pull request introduces significant updates to the HL7v2 library, focusing on improving the API design, simplifying the codebase, and enhancing the documentation. Key changes include replacing the `HL7v2Message` class with a new `HL7v2Client` class, updating the README to reflect the new API, and refactoring the test suite to align with the updated implementation.

### API Redesign and Refactoring:
* Replaced the `HL7v2Message` class with the new `HL7v2Client` class, which provides a cleaner and more extensible API for parsing HL7v2 messages. This includes support for custom delimiters, detailed error handling, and stateless design. (`src/client.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `src/message.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-25d66d74617fe2e23d7946bd6e3ba95640ab1b9bc8947445d604fc271c7c1f12R1-R189) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a2a171449d862fe29692ce031981047d7ab755ae7f84c707aef80701b3ea0c80L1-R1) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-60ea006d358dc5cddec873646d6aaae8ee58e5dcee845e71069a25b99ba126bbL1-L216)

### Documentation Updates:
* Updated `README.md` to reflect the new `HL7v2Client` API, emphasizing type safety, functional design, and improved feature descriptions. Removed outdated content and added detailed usage examples. (`README.md`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L1-R66) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L72-L76)

### Test Suite Updates:
* Refactored the test suite to align with the new `HL7v2Client` class, including updates to test cases for parsing, field access, components, and repeats. Renamed the test file to match the new implementation. (`src/test/client.test.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6f24c5bc638e6a371d1a5cc0f387778379b5828b35f3ff5414a63821bf267958L2-R30) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6f24c5bc638e6a371d1a5cc0f387778379b5828b35f3ff5414a63821bf267958L60-R98) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6f24c5bc638e6a371d1a5cc0f387778379b5828b35f3ff5414a63821bf267958L119-R129)

These changes streamline the library's functionality, improve usability, and ensure consistency across the codebase and documentation.

author: xerial
body:
## Release v0.2.0

### 🎉 New Features

#### CDP (Customer Data Platform) Support (Experimental)
- Added 4 new MCP tools for CDP operations:
  - `list_parent_segments`: List all parent segments in your CDP account
  - `get_parent_segment`: Get details of a specific parent segment
  - `list_segments`: List segments under a parent segment
  - `list_activations`: List activations (syndications) for a segment
- CDP client with TD1 authentication and multi-site support
- Comprehensive tests including integration tests against dev environment
- Note: CDP tools are marked as experimental and currently support read-only operations

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
- Hide 'dev' site from error messages to avoid exposing internal environments (#48)

### 🔧 Improvements
- CDP tools now return structured JSON data for consistency with other tools (#49)
- All tools follow the same JSON output pattern for better programmatic consumption

### 📚 Documentation
- Added CDP documentation to README with usage examples
- Updated CLAUDE.md with CDP integration details
- Marked CDP features as experimental with notes about limitations (#50)

### 🔐 Security
- CDP API keys are properly masked in error messages
- CDP operations are included in audit logging

### Technical Details
- CDP endpoints follow the same site pattern as Trino endpoints
- Uses existing TD_API_KEY and TD_SITE configuration
- No additional environment variables required

### Version Updates
- Bumped package.json version from 0.1.10 to 0.2.0
- Updated server version identifier

---

This release introduces experimental CDP support, allowing AI assistants to interact with Treasure Data's Customer Data Platform features through the Model Context Protocol.

## ❓무슨 문제가 발생했나요 ?

## 💬 논의 사항

<!-- 논의하고 싶은 사항을 적어 주시고, 토론이 필요하시면 토론 탭에 추가 부탁드립니다. -->

## 💬 기타 참고 사항
- 페이지 UI만 구현, 기능은 추후 추가할 예정입니다.
- 구성원, 초대내역 리스트는 map을 이용해 구현하였는데, 임시 데이터를 삭제하며 현재는 내부에서 return 한 li 값만 남겨두었습니다. 이 부분은 나중에 구성원리스트, 초대내역리스트로 따로 컴포넌트로 빼려고 합니다.
- 구성원에서 프로필 이미지가 있는 경우, 프로필 이미지가 없는 경우 구분을 위해 profileImgUrl 임시 지정하였습니다. 
- UI 확인을 위해 임시 설정한 값은 커밋한 코드에서는 다시 삭제하였습니다. (사이드바 너비, 구성원 mockdata, 초대내역 mockdata)
- 시맨틱 태그 올바르게 사용 한 건지 확인 부탁드립니다!

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **신규 기능**
  - 대시보드 편집 페이지가 완전히 새롭게 구성되어, 대시보드 이름, 색상 선택, 멤버 관리, 초대 내역 확인, 페이지네이션, 변경 사항 저장 및 삭제 버튼 등 다양한 UI 요소가 추가되었습니다.

  - 페이지네이션 버튼에 배경색이 흰색으로 적용되어 시각적 구분이 강화되었습니다.

author: jra3
body:
## Summary
This PR optimizes both member and species search functionality by moving filtering logic from JavaScript to the database level, resulting in significant performance improvements.

## Changes

### Member Search Optimization
- Added `searchMembers()` database function with SQL LIKE queries
- Replaced `getRoster()` + in-memory filtering with direct database search
- Added database index on `display_name` column (migration 005)
- Only loads matching records instead of all members

### Species Search Optimization  
- Created `searchSpeciesTypeahead()` function with database-level LIMIT for typeahead searches
- Simplified LIKE comparisons by removing redundant genus/species checks (since scientific_name already contains these)
- Added database indexes on `common_name`, `scientific_name`, and `group_id` columns (migration 006)
- Typeahead queries now limit results at database level instead of using JavaScript `.slice()`

## Performance Benefits
- **Before**: Load all records into memory, then filter in JavaScript
- **After**: Database executes indexed queries, returns only matching records
- Scales much better as the database grows
- Lower memory usage and faster response times
- Indexes improve search performance (though LIKE with leading % has limitations)

## Database Changes
- Migration 005: Adds index on `members.display_name`
- Migration 006: Adds indexes on `species_name.common_name`, `species_name.scientific_name`, and `species_name.group_id`
- Updated `schema.sql` to reflect new indexes

## Testing
- All existing tests pass
- API contracts remain unchanged
- Backward compatibility maintained

<details>

   ### 7.9.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a ``[run] core`` configuration setting to specify the measurement core,
  which was previously only available through the COVERAGE_CORE environment
  variable. Finishes `issue 1746`_.

- Fixed incorrect rendering of f-strings with doubled braces, closing `issue
  1980`_.

- If the C tracer core can't be imported, a warning ("no-ctracer") is issued
  with the reason.

- The C tracer core extension module now conforms to `PEP 489`_, closing `issue
  1977`_.  Thanks, `Adam Turner <pull 1978_>`_.

- Fixed a "ValueError: min() arg is an empty sequence" error caused by strange
  empty modules, found by `oss-fuzz`_.

  1942`_.  Thanks, `Jeremy Fleischman <pull 1943_>`_.

- Fix: the PYTHONSAFEPATH environment variable new in Python 3.11 is properly
  supported, closing `issue 1696`_.  Thanks, `Philipp A. <pull 1700_>`_.  This
  works properly except for a detail when using the ``coverage`` command on
  Windows.  There you can use ``python -m coverage`` instead if you need exact
  emulation.

.. _issue 1696: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1696
.. _pull 1700: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1700
.. _issue 1942: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1942
.. _pull 1943: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1943

.. _changes_7-7-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.7.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- A few small tweaks to the sys.monitoring support for Python 3.14.  Please
  test!


.. _changes_7-7-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.7.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- The Coverage object has a new method, :meth:`.Coverage.branch_stats` for
  getting simple branch information for a module.  Closes `issue 1888`_.

- The :class:`Coverage constructor<.Coverage>` now has a ``plugins`` parameter
  for passing in plugin objects directly, thanks to `Alex Gaynor <pull
  1919_>`_.

- Many constant tests in if statements are now recognized as being optimized
  away.  For example, previously ``if 13:`` would have been considered a branch
  with one path not taken.  Now it is understood as always true and no coverage
  is missing.

- The experimental sys.monitoring support now works for branch coverage if you
  are using Python 3.14.0 alpha 6 or newer.  This should reduce the overhead
  coverage.py imposes on your test suite. Set the environment variable
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` to try it out.

- Confirmed support for PyPy 3.11. Thanks Michał Górny.

.. _issue 1888: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1888
.. _pull 1919: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1919


.. _changes_7-6-12:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.12
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some aarch64 distributions were missing (`issue 1927`_).  These are now
  building reliably.

.. _issue 1927: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1927

.. _changes_7-6-11:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.11
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: a memory leak in CTracer has been fixed.  The details are in `issue
  1924`_ and `pytest-dev 676`_.  This should reduce the memory footprint for
  everyone even if it hadn't caused a problem before.

- We now ship a py3-none-any.whl wheel file.  Thanks, `Russell Keith-Magee
  <pull 1914_>`_.

.. _pull 1914: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1914
.. _issue 1924: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1924
.. _pytest-dev 676: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/676

.. _changes_7-6-10:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.10
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some descriptions of missing branches in HTML and LCOV reports were
  incorrect when multi-line statements were involved (`issue 1874`_ and `issue
  1875`_).  These are now fixed.

- Fix: Python 3.14 `defers evaluation of annotations <pep649_>`_ by moving them
  into separate code objects.  That code is rarely executed, so coverage.py
  would mark them as missing, as reported in `issue 1908`_.  Now they are
  ignored by coverage automatically.

- Fixed an obscure and mysterious problem on PyPy 3.10 seemingly involving
  mocks, imports, and trace functions: `issue 1902`_.  To be honest, I don't
  understand the problem or the solution, but ``git bisect`` helped find it,
  and now it's fixed.

- Docs: re-wrote the :ref:`subprocess` page to put multiprocessing first and to
  highlight the correct use of :class:`multiprocessing.Pool
  <python:multiprocessing.pool.Pool>`.

.. _issue 1874: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1874

- Fix: the LCOV report code assumed that a branch line that took no branches
  meant that the entire line was unexecuted.  This isn't true in a few cases:

  Fixes `issue 1896`_.

- Fix: similarly, the HTML report will now explain that a line that jumps to
  none of its expected destinations must have always raised an exception.
  Previously, it would say something nonsensical like, "line 4 didn't jump to
  line 5 because line 4 was never true, and it didn't jump to line 7 because
  line 4 was always true."  This was also shown in `issue 1896`_.

author: johnpaix-ez1
body:
This commit implements a series of changes to address:
1.  Original `ValueError` with Wav2Vec2 `output_attentions` and "sdpa".
2.  `OutOfMemoryError` during `.cpu()` call in `generate.py`.
3.  General GPU memory hygiene.

Detailed changes:

**Part A: Reverted to 'sdpa-friendly' Attention Settings**
    - `models/wav2vec2.py`: Modified `Wav2VecModel` to not forcefully enable `self.config.output_attentions = True`. Instead, it respects the `output_attentions` argument from the caller, defaulting to the Hugging Face model's original configuration if not specified. This allows the use of efficient "sdpa" attention when attentions are not explicitly needed.
    - `models/float/FLOAT.py`: Removed `attn_implementation="eager"` from the `Wav2VecModel.from_pretrained()` call in `AudioEncoder`. This allows the Transformers library to select the default, typically "sdpa", attention mechanism.

**Part B: Implemented One-by-One CPU Frame Transfer (OOM Fix)**
    - `models/float/FLOAT.py`: Modified the `decode_latent_into_image` method in the `FLOAT` class. Generated frames (on GPU) are now immediately moved to CPU one by one within the generation loop and collected in a list. The final tensor is then stacked from these CPU tensors, significantly reducing peak GPU memory.
    - `generate.py`: Updated the `run_inference` method in `InferenceAgent` to correctly handle the fact that the frame tensor (`d_hat`) received from `FLOAT.py` is now already on the CPU. The problematic `.cpu()` call on the full frames tensor has been removed.

**Part C: Added Final Memory Cleanup Calls**
    - `nodes.py`: In the `FloatProcess` class's `floatprocess` method, within the `finally` block (after temporary file deletion), added calls to `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` (if CUDA is available) and `gc.collect()` to encourage resource release after the node's execution.

These changes collectively improve the robustness, memory efficiency, and stability of the ComfyUI-FLOAT integration.

author: fabiomigueldp
body:
This commit introduces a system-wide fullscreen mode toggle in AuraOS.

Key changes:
- I added a fullscreen toggle button to the Top Bar (`index.html`).
  - The button includes "enter" and "exit" fullscreen SVG icons.
- I implemented JavaScript logic (`index.html`):
  - This handles button clicks to enter/exit browser native fullscreen.
  - It listens to `fullscreenchange` events to update button icon and tooltip.
  - It manages an `is-fullscreen` class on the button for styling.
- I added CSS styles (`index.html`):
  - These style the new fullscreen button for consistency with existing UI elements.
  - They hide the Top Bar and Dock with a fade-out transition when in fullscreen mode (`html:fullscreen`).
  - They toggle icon visibility based on the `is-fullscreen` class.
- I updated `WindowManager.js`:
  - I modified `getWorkArea()` to return full screen dimensions (`window.innerWidth`, `window.innerHeight`) when `document.fullscreenElement` is active. This ensures maximized windows utilize the entire screen space in fullscreen mode.

This feature enhances your experience by providing an immersive environment, particularly for applications like games or media viewers, by hiding system UI elements and maximizing usable screen space.

author: djr7c4
body:
By default chatgpt-shell-anthropic-thinking-budget-tokens is 32000. This exceeds
the maximum number of tokens for some models (e.g. Opus 4) and is a pain since
the maximum number of tokens differs across different anthropic models. This PR
allows a value of 'max which uses as many thinking tokens as possible.

author: ue2020
body:
This PR adds a UI control to Tenebra GTK for configuring the `windows_capture_api` option, which is an existing feature in the core Tenebra binary. This makes the setting easily accessible to users without requiring them to manually edit the configuration file.

#### Motivation

The core Tenebra application already supports two different screen capture APIs on Windows to enhance compatibility:

*   **Windows Graphics Capture (WGC):** The modern, default API.
*   **DXGI Desktop Duplication:** A fallback API that can resolve issues on certain systems or driver configurations.

Currently, switching between these APIs requires a manual edit of `config.toml`. This PR exposes that setting in the GUI, making it straightforward for users to select the capture method that works best for them.

#### Changes Implemented

*   **UI Control:** A new `AdwComboRow` (dropdown menu) labeled "Windows capture API" has been added to the settings view.
*   **Platform Specificity:** The new widget is conditionally compiled and is only enabled on Windows builds, as the underlying Tenebra option is platform-specific.
*   **Configuration Management:** The `save()` and `refresh()` functions have been updated to correctly read and write the `windows_capture_api` key to `config.toml`, ensuring the user's choice is persisted.

**Note:** This change only affects the Tenebra GTK configurator. It does not alter any of the capture logic within the Tenebra binary itself; it simply provides a GUI to control an existing option.

#### How to Test

1.  Build and run the application on a **Windows** machine.
2.  Navigate to the settings page.
3.  Confirm that the "Windows capture API" dropdown is present and enabled, with "wgc" selected by default.
4.  Select "dxgi" and save the settings.
5.  Open `C:\tenebra\config.toml` and verify the line `windows_capture_api = "dxgi"` is present.
6.  Restart Tenebra GTK and confirm the dropdown correctly shows "dxgi" as the selected option.
7.  Start the Tenebra service and verify (via logs or behavior, if possible) that it is using the selected API.

body:
## Summary

This PR introduces comprehensive multi-currency support and shipping cost calculation features to the Android OpenTelemetry demo app, along with improved telemetry patterns and API compatibility fixes.

### Key Features Added
• **Multi-Currency Support**: 33+ currencies with persistent selection and real-time price conversion
• **Dynamic Shipping Costs**: Real-time shipping calculation based on checkout preview API
• **Enhanced UI Components**: Currency toggle, full currency picker with search, improved checkout flow
• **Comprehensive Telemetry**: Currency operations, shipping calculations, and user interaction tracking

### Technical Improvements
• **Resource Management**: Added comprehensive documentation on use blocks for automatic span lifecycle management
• **API Compatibility**: Fixed deprecated Divider() and statusBarColor usage for modern Android APIs
• **Architecture Documentation**: Enhanced ARCHITECTURE.md with detailed patterns for exception-safe telemetry
• **Client-Side Cart**: Mobile-optimized cart architecture with immediate UI updates

### Currency & Shipping Features
• **Currency Selection**: Quick toggle for major currencies + full picker for all supported currencies
• **Persistent Preferences**: Currency selection stored in SharedPreferences with USD default
• **Real-time Pricing**: All product APIs support `?currencyCode=` parameter for dynamic pricing
• **Shipping Integration**: Uses checkout API preview mode for accurate shipping cost calculation
• **Localized Display**: Proper currency symbols and formatting for major currencies

### OpenTelemetry Enhancements
• **Use Block Patterns**: Automatic span lifecycle management with exception safety
• **Currency Telemetry**: Track currency selection events and pricing operations
• **Shipping Telemetry**: Monitor shipping calculation timing and success rates
• **Enhanced Context**: Improved span attributes for currency and shipping operations

### Architecture Documentation
• **Resource Management Patterns**: Comprehensive documentation on Kotlin use blocks for OpenTelemetry spans
• **Exception Safety**: Examples of automatic span closure and status setting
• **Best Practices**: Implementation patterns for robust telemetry collection

## Implementation Details

### Multi-Currency Support
- **API Integration**: All product endpoints support `?currencyCode=` parameter
- **UI Components**: 
  - `CurrencyToggle`: Quick access to USD, EUR, GBP, JPY in product header
  - `CurrencyBottomSheet`: Full searchable picker for all 33+ currencies
- **State Management**: `CurrencyViewModel` handles selection, persistence, and API integration
- **Formatting**: Localized currency display with proper symbols and fallback patterns

### Shipping Cost Calculation
- **Preview API**: Uses checkout endpoint with preview flag to calculate shipping without order placement
- **Real-time Updates**: Shipping costs update automatically when shipping info is complete
- **Currency Integration**: Shipping costs displayed in selected currency
- **Error Handling**: Graceful degradation when shipping API unavailable

### Telemetry Enhancements
- **Automatic Resource Management**: Use blocks ensure spans are properly closed
- **Exception Safety**: Span status automatically set on success/failure
- **Rich Attributes**: Currency codes, shipping costs, and user interaction context
- **Performance Monitoring**: Track currency switching and shipping calculation performance

## Test plan

- [x] Build passes without deprecation warnings
- [x] Currency selection persists across app restarts
- [x] Shipping costs calculate correctly in different currencies
- [x] Telemetry data appears in Honeycomb with proper currency/shipping attributes
- [x] UI responds immediately to currency changes
- [x] Checkout flow works end-to-end with selected currency and calculated shipping
- [x] All existing demo scenarios still function (crashes, ANRs, slow renders)
- [x] Use block patterns properly handle exceptions and resource cleanup
- [x] Architecture documentation provides clear implementation guidance

This pull request introduces a new `Email` page and integrates it into the application, while also making adjustments to navigation and contact options. The most significant changes include adding the `Email` component, updating the routing to include the new page, and modifying the `Contact` page to link to the `Email` page instead of using a direct email link.

### New `Email` Page:

* [`src/components/Pages/Email.js`](diffhunk://#diff-424cae0bd43e8e0bbbc3f62c224a2a401c929474c574874cf544c61dec534b0dR1-R284): Added a new `Email` component with modern styling, Formspree integration for handling form submissions, and dynamic CSS animations. This component allows users to send messages via a form and displays a success message upon submission.

--- ## Remediation This change fixes "OS commands should not be vulnerable to command injection attacks" (id = [pythonsecurity:S2076](https://rules.sonarsource.com/python/RSPEC-2076/)) identified by Sonar. ## Details This codemod sandboxes all instances of [subprocess.run](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.run) and [subprocess.call](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.call) to offer protection against attack. Left unchecked, `subprocess.run` and `subprocess.call` can execute any arbitrary system command. If an attacker can control part of the strings used as program paths or arguments, they could execute arbitrary programs, install malware, and anything else they could do if they had a shell open on the application host. Our change introduces a sandbox which protects the application: ```diff import subprocess + from security import safe_command ... - subprocess.run("echo 'hi'", shell=True) + safe_command.run(subprocess.run, "echo 'hi'", shell=True) ... - subprocess.call(["ls", "-l"]) + safe_command.call(subprocess.call, ["ls", "-l"]) ``` The default `safe_command` restrictions applied are the following: * **Prevent command chaining**. Many exploits work by injecting command separators and causing the shell to interpret a second, malicious command. The `safe_command` functions attempt to parse the given command, and throw a `SecurityException` if multiple commands are present. * **Prevent arguments targeting sensitive files.** There is little reason for custom code to target sensitive system files like `/etc/passwd`, so the sandbox prevents arguments that point to these files that may be targets for exfiltration. There are [more options for sandboxing](https://github.com/pixee/python-security/blob/main/src/security/safe_command/api.py#L5) if you are interested in locking down system commands even more. ## Dependency Updates This codemod relies on an external dependency. We have automatically added this dependency to your project's `requirements.txt` file. This library holds security tools for protecting Python API calls. author: copilot
body:
The `reviewers` field in `dependabot.yml` is being deprecated by GitHub and will be removed soon. According to the [GitHub changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-04-29-dependabot-reviewers-configuration-option-being-replaced-by-code-owners/), reviewers should now be specified using the CODEOWNERS file instead.

This PR removes the deprecated `reviewers` configuration from both package ecosystems:
- Removed `reviewers` field from npm package ecosystem configuration
- Removed `reviewers` field from github-actions package ecosystem configuration

The CODEOWNERS file already exists and is properly configured with `@KevinTCoughlin` as the owner for all files (`*`), so Dependabot PRs will continue to have the same reviewer automatically assigned.

**Changes:**
- Removed 4 lines total from `.github/dependabot.yml`
- No functional changes - reviewers will still be assigned via CODEOWNERS
- All existing tests pass and linting is clean

Fixes #334.

author: beninato8
body:
This PR addresses the changes requested in #346 from earlier this year, as I also would like to be able to use this feature.

It adds 2 new outputs: CACHE-HIT and PUB-CACHE-HIT. These just pass along the `cache-hit` output from `actions/cache@v4` for the `cache-flutter` and `cache-pub` steps. These can be used for increasing workflow efficiency through steps like conditionally installing dependencies when the cache is invalid. The README is also updated with example usage to skip `melos bootstrap` if `PUB-CACHE-HIT` was not `true`.

I tested the outputs here: https://github.com/beninato8-forks/flutter-action/actions/runs/15627281250/job/44023816175

```
Cache restored successfully
Cache restored from key: flutter-linux-stable-3.27.4-x64-d8a9f9a52e5af486f80d932e838ee93861ffd863
...
Cache restored successfully
Cache restored from key: flutter-pub-linux-stable-3.27.4-x64-d8a9f9a52e5af486f80d932e838ee93861ffd863-
...
Cache Hit: true
Pub Cache Hit: true
```

Output from the following steps (after a previous run was cached):
```
- name: Flutter Action 1
  uses: ./
  id: flutter-action-1
  with:
    flutter-version: '3.27.x'
    channel: 'stable'
    cache: true

- name: Print Action Outputs 1
  run: |
    echo "Cache Hit: ${{ steps.flutter-action-1.outputs.CACHE-HIT }}"
    echo "Pub Cache Hit: ${{ steps.flutter-action-1.outputs.PUB-CACHE-HIT }}"
```

This PR closes #346

author: duizendstra
body:
This Pull Request finalizes and merges all feature work and documentation updates for the `v0.2.0` release.

This release, themed **"Process & Governance Refinement,"** marks a significant step in maturing the THEA framework. It moves us from a foundational set of artifacts to a project with well-defined, documented, and repeatable processes for contribution and continuous improvement.

This PR follows the procedure outlined in the [Framework Release Playbook](thea/application-guides/playbooks/process_guidance/framework-release-playbook.md).

### Key Changes in This Release

#### Added

*   **New Governance Playbooks:**
    *   `contribution-and-improvement-playbook.md`: Defines the end-to-end process for community and team contributions using GitHub Issues.
    *   `puzzle-assembly-playbook.md`: Establishes the "Puzzle Philosophy" for understanding the ContextVibes ecosystem.
    *   `ai-led-research-playbook.md`: Formalizes the process for commissioning research.
*   **New Lessons Learned Process:** Implemented a formal process for capturing key insights, with an initial document establishing front matter exceptions for repository-facing files.

#### Changed

*   **Metadata Overhaul:** Audited and updated the YAML front matter for 9 core framework documents to ensure full compliance with our schema, significantly improving the framework's machine-readability.
*   **Contribution Guidelines:** Refined `.github/CONTRIBUTING.MD` to align with the new, issue-driven contribution playbook.
*   **Policy Establishment:** Formalized the policy to exclude files like `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` from front matter indexing to ensure proper rendering on GitHub.

#### Fixed

*   **Inconsistent Metadata:** Corrected and completed metadata across numerous key documents, resolving inconsistencies.

### Next Steps

A final pre-merge check has been completed on the `release/v0.2.0` branch.

Once this PR is merged into `main`, the `v0.2.0` tag will be created and pushed to officially finalize the release.

cc @Orion @Athena for final review and approval.

author: huulinhnguyen-dev
body:
Fixes #
Fix the issue https://github.com/dotnet/msbuild/issues/10007 the message just display the  name of the metadata that holds the parameter value but not display the name of the attribute type whose definition it did not find
### Context
When using the MSBuild with `WriteCodeFragment` in .csproj file, if the positional constructor parameters, use metadata names that resemble `_Parameter1`, `_Parameter2` and the Attribute cannot found, the message display `"Could not infer the type of parameter "1" because the attribute type is unknown. The value will be treated as a string" instead of the name of the parameters"`

### Changes Made
Add the name of the attribute type into the message when the definitions cannot find

### Testing
Build a .csproj file with WriteCodeFragment and using an Attribute cannot found with and the message display look like this
`Could not infer the type of parameter "_Parameter1" because the attribute type "System.TheAttributeCannotFound" is unknown. The value will be treated as a string.`

### Notes

body:
#21027 

## 🛠️ PR Summary

<sub>Made with ❤️ by [Ultralytics Actions](https://github.com/ultralytics/actions)<sub>

### 🌟 Summary
Adds real-time streaming of detection results between devices using simple socket methods, enabling distributed and remote YOLO workflows. 🚀🔗

### 📊 Key Changes
- Introduced `send_to_peer()` method in the `Results` class to send detection results as JSON over TCP to another device.
- Added `receive_from_peer()` utility to listen for and collect incoming detection results on a specified network port.
- Updated documentation with clear usage examples for setting up sender and receiver devices.
- Expanded the list of `Results` methods in the docs to include the new streaming capability.

### 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **Enables distributed inference:** Easily stream YOLO detection results to remote servers, dashboards, or other devices for real-time monitoring or processing.
- **Simplifies multi-device pipelines:** Facilitates collaboration between edge devices and cloud systems without complex setup.
- **User-friendly integration:** Minimal code changes required; just call `send_to_peer()` and `receive_from_peer()` as shown in the docs.
- **Great for remote logging and dashboards:** Perfect for scenarios like live monitoring, remote logging, or cloud-based visualization of results.

This update makes it much easier to build scalable, real-time YOLO applications across multiple devices! 🌐✨

author: ofonmbuka
body:
**Description:**
This pull request introduces a comprehensive protocol upgrade focused on platform consistency, scalability, and user safety. The changes are structured across four key areas:

---

### Standardization & Platform Limits

* **Added**: `ErrorCodes` and `StatusConstants` for unified error handling and state management.
* **Defined**: `PlatformLimits` for actions, batch sizes, and content to ensure system scalability and predictability.

---

### Identity, Privacy & Safety

* **Introduced**:

  * `Users`: Core identity registry with metadata and reputation tracking.
  * `UserPrivacy`: Fine-grained visibility settings for user content and presence.
  * `BlockedUsers`: Multi-layered user safety mechanisms.
  * `Friendships`: Social graph with interaction tracking.

* **Validators**:

  * `user-exists`, `check-active-user`, and `is-blocked` for access control and trust enforcement.

---

### Rate Limiting & Admin Control

* **Implemented**:

  * `RateLimits`, `check-rate-limit`, `update-rate-limit`: Granular, extensible rate limiting.
  * `PlatformConfig`: Centralized configuration for admin-level platform governance.

---

### Content & Engagement Analytics

* **Added**:

  * `UserContent`: Tracks user-generated posts/messages.
  * `UserActivity`: Tracks engagement, action streaks, and behavior.
  * `UserBatches`: Optimizes batch processing strategies.
  * `calculate-reputation`: Dynamic trust scoring engine.

* **Utilities**:

  * `max-uint`, `min-uint` for performance optimization.
  * `are-friends` validator to streamline relationship-based logic.

---

**Impact:**
This protocol layer update improves:

* System **consistency** and **error resilience**.
* **Scalability** via defined limits and batch optimizations.
* **User trust and safety** through validation, blocking, and privacy.
* **Administrative control** and platform governance.
* **Analytics and engagement visibility** for future recommendation and moderation systems.

author: mitschabaude
body:
As the title says -- I didn't like that we copied variables just to make the output of bit rotation gadgets easier to deal with. In fact, the concrete value of a circuit's output rarely matters in parent circuits, and a reasonable strategy to reduce complexity is to wrap the output in a method that parent circuits never have to unfold.

* Abstract away output of bit rotation and general rotation gadgets
* Adapt many hard-coded offsets in Keccak elaborated circuits, since we reduced the number of variables
* Adapt and simplify Blake3 G proof

author: joka921
body:
For far, `CompressedRelation::getFirstAndLastBlock` read the first and last block of the given range `metadataAndBlocks` in order to determine the first and last triple. However, when there are updates, all the triples in a block might be deleted, so we have to find the first non-empty block from the beginning and from the end of the range. In the typical case, when both the first and the last block of the given range are non-empty, the time complexity of the function does not increase.

NOTE: For large relations, the reading of the first and last block could be saved by looking up the respective information in the (augmented) metadata. However, we don't expect a significant performance gain from that; see the discussion at the end of the PR.

## New Venue Submission

**Venue:** The Rock House
**Location:** Rockhouse State Memorial, 3663 Country Club Rd, Sparta, TN 38583
**Submitted by:** Resin
**Website:** https://www.tn.gov/historicalcommission/state-programs/state-historic-sites/sparta-rock-house.html

### Description
The small, stone Rock House, originally built to collect tolls on a private road, was built between 1835 and 1839 by Barlow Fiske, who operated a stage coach inn and stables nearby.

It played an important role in the early development of Tennessee's transportation system. Andrew Jackson often stopped here on trips from Nashville to Washington. Other notable visitors included James K. Polk, Sam Houston, and Frank Clement, all once governors of the Volunteer State.

<!-- Add any other context or information about the pull request that might be helpful, such as related PRs, references, discussions, etc. -->
The `storageMode` parameter has been removed from the iOS `Configuration` to ensure consistency between the Kotlin and Swift SDKs. In the first stable release of the Kotlin SDK, no storage-related parameters are exposed to the client. To maintain this parity, the iOS SDK has been updated accordingly. Previously, the `storageMode` parameter allowed clients to choose between disk and memory for event storage. This option is now internal to the SDK.

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses the optimization of the `bus2to1.v` module by fixing critical blocking assignment issues and implementing proper bus crossbar functionality with queuing and fair arbitration.

## Issues Fixed

### 1. Blocking Mux Signals (Critical Bug)
The original code contained combinational loops that caused blocking behavior:
```verilog
// OLD - Creates combinational loop
assign m1_rdata = rs_qm1 ? s_rdata : m1_rdata;
assign m2_rdata = rs_qm2 ? s_rdata : m2_rdata;

// NEW - Clean assignments with buffering
assign m1_rdata = m1_rdata_valid ? m1_rdata_reg : 32'h0;
assign m2_rdata = m2_rdata_valid ? m2_rdata_reg : 32'h0;
```

### 2. Improved Bus Crossbar Architecture
- **Fair Arbitration**: Implemented round-robin arbitration with `fair_toggle` to prevent master starvation
- **Proper State Machine**: Replaced simple priority logic with robust IDLE/GRANT_M1/GRANT_M2 states
- **Read Data Buffering**: Added `m1_rdata_reg`/`m2_rdata_reg` with validity tracking for pipeline optimization
- **Standard Clocking**: Changed from unusual `negedge clk` to standard `posedge clk` for better timing

### 3. Enhanced Bus Functionality
- **Non-blocking Operation**: Masters can now queue requests without blocking each other
- **Transaction Integrity**: Proper completion detection with `grant & valid & ready` conditions
- **Queuing Support**: Read data buffering provides the foundation for more advanced queuing

## Key Technical Changes

1. **Arbitration Logic**: 
   - State machine with proper IDLE/GRANT states
   - Fair round-robin prevents starvation when both masters compete
   - Transaction-based grant management

2. **Data Path Optimization**:
   - Eliminated combinational loops in read data paths
   - Added buffering with validity tracking
   - Improved timing characteristics

3. **Interface Compatibility**:
   - Maintains same module interface as original
   - Compatible with existing `vigna_top.v` integration
   - Preserves all functionality while fixing critical issues

## Testing
The optimized module maintains full backward compatibility while providing the enhanced bus crossbar functionality requested. The changes transform the simple mux into a proper reality bus with queuing and optimization features.

Fixes #3.

author: petertzy
body:
The test code in Laravel Excel uses the legacy model factory syntax, which has been removed by default in Laravel 8 and above.
To make the tests pass, we need to install the `laravel/legacy-factories` package.

Run the following command:

```bash
composer require --dev laravel/legacy-factories
```

This package is officially provided by Laravel as a compatibility tool for the old factory syntax, and it works well with `orchestra/testbench`.

After installation, run the tests again:

```bash
vendor/bin/phpunit
```

The result should be:

```
Time: 02:22.138, Memory: 98.50 MB

OK (331 tests, 1405 assertions)
```

Running the tests will generate a `.phpunit.cache` directory.
Make sure to add it to `.gitignore`:

```
.phpunit.cache
```

author: andrewleech
body:
## Summary

Changes Python session state preservation to be the default behavior in mpremote. Previously, mpremote performed automatic soft-reset between command sessions, clearing variables and imports. Users had to explicitly use the `resume` command to preserve state.

This change makes the "resume" behavior the default and removes the `resume` command entirely. Users wanting the old auto soft-reset behavior can now explicitly add `soft-reset` to their command sequences.

**Example behavior change:**
```bash
# Before (auto soft-reset default):
mpremote exec "a = 1" eval "a"  # Would fail with NameError
mpremote resume exec "a = 1" eval "a"  # Would work

# After (resume default):
mpremote exec "a = 1" eval "a"  # Now works by default
mpremote soft-reset exec "a = 1" eval "a"  # Explicit soft-reset for old behavior
```

## Testing

- Updated existing `test_resume.sh` test to reflect new behavior
- All pre-commit hooks pass (ruff, codespell, codeformat.py)
- Tested that explicit `soft-reset` commands replicate the old default behavior

## Trade-offs and Alternatives

**Benefits:**
- More intuitive behavior - variables persist as users expect
- Reduces need for explicit `resume` commands in workflows
- Simplifies automation scripts that work with persistent state

**Breaking change considerations:**
- Existing scripts expecting auto soft-reset will see different behavior
- Some users may have automation that depends on clean state per command
- Migration path: add explicit `soft-reset` where clean state is required

**Implementation details:**
- Changed `State.__init__()` to set `_auto_soft_reset = False` by default
- Removed `do_resume()` function and command registration
- Removed auto-reset on disconnect to maintain consistency
- Explicit `soft-reset` command continues to work as before

This provides the same functionality as before but with inverted defaults, making the more commonly desired behavior (state persistence) the default while still allowing users to get clean state when needed.

author: ms-ethomaso
body:
Issue: with one of my gitlab pipelines, our usage of service directives over parallel executors was causing nodejs errors to be raised when trying to replace dockerCmd strings that for some reason were not strings.

Solution: Force casting the values to be string representations in all cases fixed the issue I was having and is a safer call to make.

author: kirre-bylund
body:
# Centralized Logging, File Logging, and HTTP Request Logging for LootLockerServerSDK

## Overview

This PR introduces a centralized and extensible logging system to the LootLockerServerSDK, bringing it in line with the feature set already present in the LootLockerSDK. The update includes a static logger class, structured HTTP request/response logging, runtime log level overrides, and file logging support.

## Key Changes

- **Refactored Logger:**  
  Replaces the UObject-based logger with a static `FLootLockerServerLogger` class, providing a more flexible and extensible logging system.

- **Structured HTTP Logging:**  
  Adds structured logging for HTTP requests and responses, including request/response data, headers, status codes, timing, and error details.

- **File Logging Support:**  
  Adds the ability to enable or disable file logging, set the log file name, and write logs to disk. File logging can be controlled at runtime or via config.

- **Runtime Log Level Override:**  
  Allows the log level to be overridden at runtime, independent of the config file.

- **Config and Blueprint Integration:**  
  Exposes logging controls (log level, file logging) via `ULootLockerServerConfig` and makes them accessible to Blueprints.

- **Editor Module Registration:**  
  Registers the `LootLockerServerSDKEditor` as an Editor module in the plugin descriptor.

## Motivation

These changes provide better diagnostics, easier debugging, and more flexible logging for both development and production environments. They also align the server SDK’s logging capabilities with those of the client SDK.

## Migration Notes

- The logger is now static and no longer a UObject.
- File logging is disabled by default and can be enabled via config or at runtime.
- Log level can be set at runtime for the current session.

## Related

- Feature parity with [LootLockerSDK PR #244](https://github.com/lootlocker/unreal-sdk/pull/244)

author: jackhodgkiss
body:
During the ``kayobe overcloud inventory discover`` command, Kayobe queries the Bifrost ironic node list and updates the Kayobe inventory. If the nodes have a driver_info.ipmi_address field set, an ipmi_address variable will be defined in the Kayobe inventory for the host.

This does not work for Redfish based hosts, which use driver_info.redfish_address in the Ironic node. This change adds a new ``redfish_address`` variable and extends the command to discover the address from the Bifrost node inventory.

Change-Id: Ieb1e61ddadb542732739d1f478b1e5a176e0ac88
